label: Treat phraseQuality pollution as a visible diagnostic advisory outside staleness_classes and severity_max; the committed bucket has 251 flagged phrases out of 33,719 (about 0.74%), so its unconditional medium severity makes a fresh corpus appear degraded and blocks a clean OK result. Keep the counts/share; do not invent a threshold or bulk-delete phrases without evidence of lookup harm.

The YAML claim that flagged phrases never rank is too broad: fewer-than-two-token phrases only fail non-exact matching, while exact equality scores 1, containment scores 0.94/0.88, and token overlap scores at query coverage >=0.8; the candidate pipeline ranks by best phrase and does not consult phraseQuality. Preserve generator diagnostics and selectively clean only demonstrated quality issues.

Update DOC-349 to expect fresh-index STATUS_OK with phraseQuality shown as an advisory and no pollution staleness class or severity; update DOC-350 so index_content_stale alone controls stale severity/recommendation while the same advisory remains visible. Keep phraseQuality generator tests; add a doctor contract test for advisory-only OK and for stale-index severity isolation.

For a recognized /doctor:mcp action, reject a flag unknown to both sub-action schemas before YAML load with ERROR="unknown_flag", the selected action, and that action’s valid flags. Preserve cross_sub_action_flag_injection for a known flag belonging only to the other action, such as --fix on install or --runtime on debug. Add the wording to mcp.md and presentation, then DOC-380 for --server.

Other doctor routers already reject unknown arguments before YAML load: git and skill-advisor reject unknown/cross-target flags; speckit rejects all other positional/flag input; env rejects unknown flags or extra selectors; runtime-mirrors accepts no arguments; deep-loop accepts only --scope; update explicitly rejects cross-action and unknown flags. This makes a dedicated mcp unknown_flag distinct from its existing cross-action error consistent.
